title: Customer-route gating: safety pilot for tiered allow/deny policies and automated rollback runbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Run a small safety pilot that applies automated per-customer / per-route optimizations (batching and prefix/KV caching adjustments) via a tiered allowlist/denylist gating policy. This ticket scopes the pilot, implements the staged apply automation, and produces a documented rollback runbook. The pilot must tie to the Optimize recommendation engine and the Console rollout API so ops can observe and abort applies. Work includes: defining segmentation predicates, building an abortable staged-apply executor, integrating telemetry-driven rollback triggers, and producing runbook + playbook for SREs and account managers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Pilot can select customers by segmentation buckets (free/prod/high-volume) and routes by pattern and apply distinct policy profiles.
2) Staged-apply executes: dry-run -> 1% canary -> 10% ramp -> full apply, and is abortable at every stage.
3) Automated rollback triggers on >25% increase in 95th pct latency, >3x error rate, or >15% net token-cost delta vs baseline within 30m.
4) Telemetry dashboards show per-tenant cost delta, latency, errors, and applied policy version.
5) Runbook and postmortem template created and reviewed by SRE and PM.
6) No data exfiltration or permission escalation introduced (security signoff).
rollout_plan: 1) Prepare policy profiles: conservative (cache-only, low batch), balanced (cache + modest batch), aggressive (batch-friendly, larger kv-prefetch). 2) Run offline simulation with 7-day traffic trace using sandbox (dry-run) and capture cost/latency estimates. 3) Create canary cohorts: 1% random, then 10% stratified by tier, then 100%. Each stage waits for 30m of steady-state telemetry. 4) If any trigger fires, automatically rollback to previous policy and notify on-call + account owner. 5) After 72h successful stability, mark pilot complete and generate recommendations for global rollout.
telemetry_queries: cost_delta_query: sum(token_cost_delta) by customer over 30m comparing policy_vN to baseline
latency_95_query: p95(latency_ms) by route and customer over 5m windows
risk_assessment: Risks: 1) Aggressive batching may increase tail latency for long-running requests — mitigated by preferring cache-first profile for latency-sensitive tiers. 2) Incorrect segmentation predicate could place high-value customers into aggressive profiles — mitigated by allowlist override for top 50 customers and manual review step during canary. 3) Telemetry lag causing delayed rollback — mitigated by using short-window alerts and conservative thresholds for first run. 4) Rollout automation bugs — gated by dry-run and manual approval before the 10% ramp.
